simple.meaning: צִידֹנִי (Tsîydônîy) appears 16 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a daughter in the family line and in connection with kingship.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, and 3 more, beginning at Deuteronomy 3:9. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, kingship, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צִידֹנִי (H6722) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows צִידֹנִי through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: צִידֹנִי (Tsîydônîy) / H6722 is tracked through Deuteronomy 3:9, Joshua 13:4, Joshua 13:6, Judges 3:3. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

timeline.evidenceText: (The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.)
on the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that belongs to the Sidonians, to Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;

all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth Maim, even all the Sidonians. I will drive them out from before the children of Israel. Just allocate it to Israel for an inheritance, as I have commanded you.
the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
The Sidonians also, and the Amalekites, and the Maonites, oppressed you; and you cried to me, and I saved you out of their hand.

Then the five men departed and came to Laish and saw the people who were there, how they lived in safety, in the way of the Sidonians, quiet and secure; for there was no one in the land possessing authority, that might put them to shame in anything, and they were far from the Sidonians, and had no dealings with anyone else.

Then the five men departed and came to Laish and saw the people who were there, how they lived in safety, in the way of the Sidonians, quiet and secure; for there was no one in the land possessing authority, that might put them to shame in anything, and they were far from the Sidonians, and had no dealings with anyone else.
Now king Solomon loved many foreign women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites;
For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.

because that they have forsaken me, and have worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon. They have not walked in my ways, to do that which is right in my eyes, and to keep my statutes and my ordinances, as David his father did.

As if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, he took as wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshiped him.

The king defiled the high places that were before Jerusalem, which were on the right hand of the mountain of corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, and for Milcom the abomination of the children of Ammon.
and cedar trees without number, for the Sidonians and the people of Tyre brought cedar trees in abundance to David.

They also gave money to the masons, and to the carpenters. They also gave food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre, to bring cedar trees from Lebanon to the sea, to Joppa, according to the grant that they had from Cyrus King of Persia.

“There are the princes of the north, all of them, and all the Sidonians, who have gone down with the slain. They are put to shame in the terror which they caused by their might. They lie uncircumcised with those who are slain by the sword, and bear their shame with those who go down to the pit.

definitions.short: a Tsidonian or inhabitant of Tsidon
definitions.full: H6722. Tsidoni צִידֹנִי adjective, of a people of foregoing; — ׳צ Judg 3:3 ; Ezek 32:30 ; elsewhere plural צִידֹנִים Deut 3:9 +, צִידוֺנִים Judg 10:12 צִדֹנִים 18:7 ; 3 t.; feminine plural צֵדְנִיֹּת 1Kin 11:1 ; — as substantive = Sidonians , coll with article Ezek 32:30 ; Judg 3:3 ; in earlier literature apparently = Phoenicians Deut 3:9 ; Josh 13:4 , 6 ; Judg 3:3 ; 10:12 ; 18:7 (twice in verse); 1 Kings 5:20 (= Tyre v. 1Kin 5:15 ), 16:31 (if, [Jos Ant. viii. 13 , 1] Ethb. was king of Tyre also), Ezek 32:30 ; also צ אְֶהֵֹי ׳עַשְׁתֹּרֶת 1Kin 11:5 , 33 , compare 2Kin 23:13 ; named with Tyrians 1Chr 22:4 ; Ezra 3:7 . צוה ציה (√ of following; Arabic be parched , so Aramaic צְוִי צְוָא (not ᵑ7 ), (chiefly in Lexicons)).
